The day after the index dropped a thousand points, my entire feed was people explaining they saw it coming.
One calls it a grey rhino, one says valuations were stretched, one digs up a post from three months ago as evidence.
I'm the only honest one here: I saw nothing coming, and I bought more that afternoon.
en.editorNote: Post this the morning after a crash, when the timeline fills up with 'I called it'
variations: The day after a selloff, the national density of prophets hits an all-time high.
In hindsight everything is a grey rhino. In real time all I saw was a wall of red.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 颱風影響台股買盤 register；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
以前颱風天，我求的是放假。
現在颱風天，我求的是休市。
只要今天不開盤，我的帳面就會永遠停在昨天那個比較體面的數字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 颱風警報發布、大家在等停班停課消息時丟進群組
variations: 我對颱風唯一的要求：來得剛好、停在星期一。
休市是老天爺給套牢族唯一的溫柔。

en.content:
Typhoon days used to mean I was praying for the office to close.
Now I'm praying the exchange closes.
If the market never opens today, my portfolio stays frozen at yesterday's slightly more dignified number.
en.editorNote: For the group chat while everyone refreshes the storm-day announcement
variations: My only request of this typhoon: perfect timing, ideally a Monday.
A market holiday is the universe's one act of mercy toward people who are underwater.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 高波動下「從追求暴利轉為控管風險」理財建議 register；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
專家說：這種洗盤行情，策略要從「追求暴利」調整成「控管風險」。
我認真對照了一下自己的狀況：暴利是完全沒追到，風險倒是控管得非常徹底——
因為我已經沒剩什麼可以再賠了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看到理財專家喊風險控管、自己卻早就被洗出場時使用
variations: 我的風險控管做得很好，方法是把本金先賠掉一半，剩下的自然就沒什麼波動。
專家的建議我全部照做，只是順序反了：我先體驗風險，再開始控管。

en.content:
The expert says: in a market this choppy, shift your strategy from 'chasing big gains' to 'managing risk.'
I checked my own situation carefully. Big gains: none chased. Risk: extremely well managed —
mostly because there isn't much left to lose.
en.editorNote: For when a finance segment lectures you about risk management and you were flushed out months ago
variations: My risk management is excellent. Step one was losing half the principal; after that the volatility really calms down.
I followed every piece of expert advice, just in the wrong order: experience the risk first, manage it later.

items.sourceNote: 2026 投資人「每九分鐘看一次看盤 APP」的行為觀察 register；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
統計說，現在的投資人平均每九分鐘就會打開一次看盤 APP。
我覺得這個數字嚴重低估。
我上一次連續九分鐘沒看，是因為人在電梯裡沒訊號。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合手機螢幕使用時間報告出來、看盤 APP 排第一名的時候
variations: 我不是一直在看盤，我只是每次解鎖手機都剛好停在那一頁。
把看盤 APP 移到最後一頁根本沒用，我的手指有肌肉記憶。

en.content:
A study says the average investor now opens their brokerage app every nine minutes.
I think that number is badly understated.
The last time I went nine straight minutes without checking, I was in an elevator with no signal.
en.editorNote: For when your weekly screen-time report puts the trading app in first place
variations: I'm not constantly checking the market. My phone just happens to unlock on that screen every time.
Moving the app to the last home screen did nothing. My thumb has muscle memory.

items.sourceNote: 技術派回測與實盤落差梗；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我的回測系統厲害到嚇死人。
過去十年的走勢丟進去，每一筆都完美低買高賣，年化報酬三位數。
然後我拿去實盤操作，才發現回測跟實盤最大的差別是——回測的時候，我早就知道明天會發生什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟給每個沉迷調參數、卻遲遲不敢真的下單的技術派朋友
variations: 回測績效越漂亮，通常代表你把參數調到剛好只認得過去那條線。
我在歷史線圖上是股神，一碰到今天這根還沒收的 K 棒就變回散戶。

en.content:
My backtesting engine is terrifyingly good.
Feed it ten years of price data and every single trade buys the bottom and sells the top. Triple-digit annual returns.
Then I ran it live and learned the one real difference between a backtest and real trading: in the backtest, I already know what tomorrow does.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps optimizing parameters but never actually places the order
variations: The prettier the backtest, the more likely you just curve-fit it to that one line from the past.
On a historical chart I'm a genius. The moment the candle in front of me hasn't closed yet, I'm retail again.

items.sourceNote: 「這次不一樣」泡沫心理經典梗；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
每一次泡沫吹到最大的時候，都會有人語重心長地跟你說：「這次不一樣。」
這句話我聽過網路股版、聽過生技版、聽過 AI 版。
每次我都信了，每次我都用真金白銀證明——不一樣的只有虧損的金額，一次比一次大。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在任何一波「這次真的會不一樣」的狂熱行情下，提醒自己先冷靜三秒
variations: 投資史上最貴的四個字，就是「這次不一樣」。
當連我這種外行都覺得「這次一定不一樣」的時候，通常就是最一樣的時候。

en.content:
Every time a bubble inflates to its peak, someone leans in and says, very sincerely, 'This time it's different.'
I've heard the dot-com version, the biotech version, the AI version.
Each time I believed it, and each time I proved it with real money — the only thing that was ever different was the size of the loss, bigger every round.
en.editorNote: Save it for the next 'this time is genuinely different' mania and give yourself three seconds to breathe
variations: The four most expensive words in investing: 'this time it's different.'
When even an amateur like me is sure this time is different, that's usually the most same it's ever been.

items.sourceNote: 把虧損合理化成「繳學費」的心理防衛梗；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
每次賠錢，我都安慰自己：這不是虧損，是繳學費。
算一算，我這幾年繳的學費，都夠念完一個博士了。
唯一的問題是，這間學校好像沒有畢業這個選項，而且每學期還自動幫我加選新的課。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給每個把停損講得很有智慧、其實只是不想承認賠錢的自己
variations: 如果虧損真的是學費，那我大概是全校最認真的學生，只是永遠考不及格。
我繳的學費早就夠多了，但這間學校從來沒發過畢業證書。

en.content:
Every time I lose money, I comfort myself: this isn't a loss, it's tuition.
Do the math and the tuition I've paid these past few years could have funded a PhD.
Only problem is, this school has no graduation option, and every semester it auto-enrolls me in a fresh set of courses.
en.editorNote: For all of us who dress up a loss as 'a lesson' to avoid admitting we just lost money
variations: If losses really are tuition, I'm the most dedicated student on campus. I just never pass the exam.
I've paid more than enough tuition. This school has simply never issued a diploma.

items.sourceNote: 「什麼都沒做的朋友反而贏」反差梗；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我研究了三年，看盤看到頭髮少一半，帳戶從六位數變五位數。
我那個什麼都不懂、只把錢放定存、連 K 線是什麼都不知道的朋友，帳戶穩穩的，一毛沒少。
原來在這個市場，最強的操作不是低買高賣，是根本沒進場。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個每次聚餐都笑你玩股票、自己卻默默存款最多的朋友
variations: 股市裡最會賺的人，有時候就是那個什麼都沒買的人。
我學了那麼多招，最後打敗我的，是一個連券商 APP 都沒下載的人。

en.content:
I studied for three years, watched charts until half my hair was gone, and turned a six-figure account into a five-figure one.
My friend — knows nothing, just parks cash in a savings account, couldn't tell a candlestick from a birthday candle — sits there untouched, not a cent lost.
Turns out the strongest move in this market isn't buying low and selling high. It's never showing up.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who teases you about trading at every dinner while quietly holding the biggest bank balance
variations: Sometimes the best-performing person in the market is the one who bought nothing at all.
I learned every trick there is, and the one who beat me never even downloaded a brokerage app.

items.sourceNote: 2026 高股息 ETF 月配息熱潮、新標的年化配息率破雙位數；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我把市值型全賣了，改抱那檔年化配息率最高的月配息 ETF，說要領被動收入，提早退休。
配息真的每個月準時入帳，我開心地截圖給家人看。
然後我打開淨值：本金縮掉的速度，比配息入帳的速度還快。
原來我領的不是被動收入，是我自己的本金，換個名字、分期發還給我而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個逢人就推「月月配、爽爽退休」的存股同事，配一張淨值走綠的截圖
variations: 所謂月配息退休夢，就是每個月很有儀式感地，領回自己一小塊本金。
我不是在領股息，我是在幫我的本金辦一場很體面的分期告別式。

en.content:
I dumped all my index funds and piled into the monthly-payout ETF with the fattest yield. Passive income, early retirement — that was the plan.
The distributions really do land in my account, right on time. I screenshot every one and send it to my family.
Then I open the NAV: my principal is shrinking faster than the payouts are arriving.
Turns out it isn't passive income. It's my own capital, renamed, handed back to me in monthly installments.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who won't stop pitching 'monthly dividends, cushy retirement' — pair it with a screenshot of the NAV in the red
variations: The monthly-dividend retirement dream is just a ceremonial ritual for getting a small piece of your own money back.
I'm not collecting a yield. I'm throwing my principal a very dignified installment funeral.

items.sourceNote: 2026 AI 狂潮「沒買 10 年後會後悔」FOMO 論述、台積電站上高檔；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
專家說：這波 AI 狂潮，現在不買，十年後一定會後悔。
我最怕後悔了，於是我當天就把台積電追在高點，把「十年後的後悔」提前結清。
現在我不用等十年了——我今天打開對帳單，當場就後悔了。
感謝專家，讓我把一個要花十年慢慢體會的情緒，一天就領完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在券商 APP 追高截圖旁，給每個被『不買會後悔』推上車的人
variations: 別人怕十年後後悔沒買，我更務實：我選擇今天先後悔買了。
我把十年份的後悔一次繳清，算是一種很有效率的情緒理財。

en.content:
The expert said: this AI wave — if you don't buy now, you'll regret it in ten years.
Regret is my worst fear, so that same day I chased the chip stock at its high and settled my 'ten-years-later regret' up front.
Now I don't have to wait a decade. I opened my statement today and regretted it on the spot.
Thank you, expert, for letting me collect ten years' worth of regret in a single afternoon.
en.editorNote: Post it next to your buy-the-top screenshot, for everyone talked onto the train by 'you'll regret not owning it'
variations: Others fear regretting not buying in ten years. I'm more practical — I chose to regret buying today.
I paid off a decade of regret in one lump sum. Call it efficient emotional portfolio management.

items.sourceNote: 2026 散戶追殖利率排行榜第一名；殖利率高常是股價先跌、分母變小；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我有一套很簡單的選股法：打開殖利率排行榜，直接買第一名。
第一名殖利率最高，代表最會賺，這不是很合理嗎？
買了幾檔以後我才想通：殖利率是股息除以股價。
它排第一名，不是因為股息特別多，是因為股價已經先崩了、分母變超小。
原來我不是在挑最會配息的，我是在專門挑那個跌最慘的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看到殖利率兩位數就眼睛發亮、直接梭哈排行榜第一名的朋友
variations: 殖利率排行榜第一名的意思，通常是『這檔股價剛剛跳樓』。
我以為我在找高殖利率，其實我是用最科學的方法，精準買在最低點的反面。

en.content:
My stock-picking system is dead simple: open the dividend-yield ranking, buy whatever's number one.
Number one has the highest yield, so it must be the best earner, right? Perfectly logical.
A few buys in, it finally clicked: yield is the dividend divided by the price.
It's ranked first not because the payout is huge, but because the price already crashed and the denominator got tiny.
Turns out I wasn't picking the best dividend payer. I was specializing in whatever had fallen the hardest.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend whose eyes light up at a double-digit yield and who goes all-in on the ranking's top name
variations: Number one on the yield ranking usually means 'this one's price just jumped off a building.'
I thought I was hunting high yield. I was actually using the most scientific method to buy the exact opposite of the bottom.

items.sourceNote: 2026 股東會紀念品旺季（聯電史努比保溫瓶、王品/大魯閣股東大禮包零股也能領）；改寫原創，為紀念品進場結果套牢

zh-tw.content:
我本來只是想領那個股東會紀念品，聽說今年送保溫瓶，市價五百塊。
為了領它，我趕在最後買進日前買了一張。
保溫瓶我領到了。
那張股票，現在帳面虧了兩萬。
我終於擁有全台灣最貴的一個保溫瓶——附贈一張捨不得賣的套牢單。
zh-tw.editorNote: 丟給每個為了紀念品下海、結果套牢的存股同好
variations: 別人買股票是為了配息，我買股票是為了那組股東會送的鍋子，現在鍋子還在，本金燒乾了。
股東會紀念品最貴的地方，從來不是紀念品本身，是那張你為了領它而買、然後再也賣不掉的股票。

en.content:
I only bought the stock to grab the shareholder-meeting gift — this year it was a thermos, retails for about fifteen bucks.
To qualify, I bought a full lot right before the cutoff.
I got the thermos.
The stock is now down six hundred dollars.
Congratulations to me: I own the most expensive thermos in the country, and it came with a share I can't bring myself to sell.
en.editorNote: For every dividend-stock friend who bought a lot just for the freebie and got stuck holding it
variations: Some people buy stocks for the dividend. I bought this one for the free cookware. The pot's still in my kitchen; the money evaporated.
The priciest part of a shareholder gift is never the gift — it's the share you bought to qualify and now can't unload.

items.sourceNote: 2026 台股新股申購：中籤率極低、備妥資金常拿到 0 股、破發率約 12%；改寫原創，抽整年沒中、好不容易中又破發

zh-tw.content:
新股申購我抽了一整年，每次都乖乖備妥錢，凍在帳戶裡等開獎。
中籤率百分之零點三，我硬是連續槓龜四十次，一張都沒中。
就在我心灰意冷、隨手多按一檔冷門股的那次——中了。
上市第一天，破發，直接跌破承銷價。
原來我的手氣不是不好，是專門用來抽那種一中就套的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在申購群組，給每個備好錢卻抽不到、好不容易抽到又破發的人
variations: 抽新股就像刮刮樂，別人刮到蜜月行情，我刮到蜜月結束後的離婚協議書。
中籤那一刻我以為中樂透，掛牌那一刻我才發現，中的是套牢的頭獎。

en.content:
I entered the IPO lottery every week for a year, dutifully parking cash in my account for each draw.
Allocation odds: 0.3%. I struck out forty times in a row — not a single share.
Then, the one time I half-heartedly tapped some boring name nobody wanted, I won.
Day one of trading: it broke below the offer price.
Turns out my luck isn't bad — it's precisely calibrated to only win the ones that trap me.
en.editorNote: For everyone in the IPO group chat who parks cash for every draw, wins nothing, then finally wins a dud
variations: IPO lotteries are like scratch cards: other people scratch a honeymoon rally, I scratch the divorce papers that come after it.
The moment I won the allocation I thought I'd hit the jackpot. The moment it listed, I realized the jackpot was getting stuck.

items.sourceNote: ETF 內扣費用（管理費/保管費每日自淨值扣除、不列在對帳單）常被新手忽略；改寫原創，區別於既有的除息/配息梗

zh-tw.content:
我買 ETF，是因為聽說被動投資最省事、成本又低，幾乎等於免費。
我從來沒在對帳單上看過任何一筆管理費，於是我很安心。
直到有人提醒我『內扣費用』這四個字——原來它不寄帳單給你，是每天默默從淨值裡先扣走。
看不到的成本，才是扣得最勤的成本。
我以為我請了一個免費的管家，其實他每天趁我沒注意，先從我皮夾拿走一點點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 丟給每個以為 ETF 零成本、忽略內扣費用的被動投資新手
variations: ETF 最厲害的地方，是它讓你完全感覺不到自己在付錢——因為它不跟你收，它直接從裡面拿。
帳單上看不到的那筆費用，不是不存在，是它聰明到不用讓你看到。

en.content:
I bought an ETF because passive investing is supposed to be effortless and cheap — practically free.
I never saw a single fee on my statement, so I slept easy.
Then someone mentioned the expense ratio: it doesn't mail you a bill, it just quietly shaves a slice off the fund's value every single day.
The cost you can't see is the one that gets collected most reliably.
I thought I'd hired a free butler. Turns out he lifts a little from my wallet each day while I'm not looking.
en.editorNote: For every passive-investing newbie who assumed an ETF was zero-cost and forgot about the expense ratio
variations: The genius of an ETF fee is that you never feel yourself paying it — because they don't charge you, they just help themselves from the inside.
The fee that never shows up on your statement isn't missing. It's just clever enough not to need to.

items.sourceNote: 現金增資：套牢股東反被公司要求按比例認購新股，不認股權稀釋、認了等於加碼虧損；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我這檔套牢兩年，已經夠委屈了。
結果公司來一封通知：辦理現金增資，請股東按比例認購新股。
翻譯成白話就是——你套牢的那間公司，現在反過來跟你討錢。
我不認，怕股權被稀釋；我認了，等於在虧損上再加碼一次。
原來這段關係最狠的不是它不漲，是它沒錢的時候，第一個想到的人是我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給每個套牢還被公司現金增資追加投資的無奈股東
variations: 談戀愛最怕遇到伸手牌，沒想到買股票也會——套牢就算了，它還發現金增資跟我要錢。
別人的股票會配息給你，我的股票會發通知跟我要錢，這大概就是所謂的『負現金流』。

en.content:
I'd been stuck in this stock for two years — humiliation enough.
Then the company sends a notice: rights issue, shareholders please subscribe to new shares pro rata.
In plain English: the company you're already trapped in is now asking you for money.
Say no, and my stake gets diluted. Say yes, and I'm doubling down on a loss.
The cruelest part of this relationship isn't that it won't go up — it's that when it runs low on cash, the first person it thinks of is me.
en.editorNote: For every underwater shareholder hit with a rights issue asking them to pony up even more
variations: The worst kind of partner is one who's always got their hand out. Turns out stocks do it too — being stuck wasn't enough, now it wants a cash injection.
Other people's stocks pay them a dividend. Mine sends a notice asking me for money. I believe the technical term is 'negative cash flow.'

items.sourceNote: 2026/3/30 新制：零股、興櫃股票也能當融資融券擔保品，媒體稱為「活化存股資產」；改寫原創，寫成拿自己的股票借錢買自己的股票

zh-tw.content:
今年有個新制上路，連零股、興櫃股票都能拿去當擔保品借錢，新聞說這叫「活化存股資產」。
我那些存了三年的零股，本來安安靜靜躺著，一動也不動，誰都沒得罪。
我把它們拿去抵押，借出一筆錢，然後用那筆錢——買了同一檔股票。
所以我現在是用我的股票，借錢買我的股票。
專家說這叫資產活化，我覺得比較像我的股票學會了自我複製，而且複製的是風險。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一聽到「零股也能質押」就眼睛發亮、準備把整份存股拿去抵押的朋友
variations: 所謂活化存股資產，就是把你原本睡得最安穩的那一份，叫起來一起加班。
我沒有多投一毛錢，我只是讓同一筆錢在帳戶裡多繞了一圈，順便多背了一份利息。

en.content:
New rule this year: even fractional shares can be pledged as collateral for a loan. The headlines call it "putting your idle holdings to work."
My fractional shares had spent three years lying there quietly, bothering absolutely no one.
So I pledged them, borrowed against them, and used the cash to buy — the exact same stock.
Which means I am now using my stock to borrow money to buy my stock.
Experts call this asset activation. It looks more like my portfolio learned to clone itself, and what it cloned was the risk.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose eyes light up at "you can borrow against fractional shares now" and is ready to pledge the whole account
variations: "Putting idle assets to work" means waking up the one part of your portfolio that was sleeping soundly and making it pull a double shift.
I didn't add a single dollar. I just made the same dollar take one extra lap around my account and pick up an interest payment on the way.

items.sourceNote: 2026 PTT 股板盤中／盤後閒聊文化：早盤空方喊崩、夜盤翻紅多方喊噴，每天重播；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我每天最固定的娛樂，是打開股板的盤中閒聊。
早上一開盤，看空的那群人開始喊：變盤了、要屠殺了、快跑啊。
下午夜盤一翻紅，看多的那群人立刻集結：噴出了、無限上看、抱緊處理。
劇情每天重播，連台詞都懶得改。
唯一有變化的是我：早上我信了空方，中午我信了多方，收盤時兩邊都對，只有我兩邊都慢了一步。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼給那個每天固定跳進盤中閒聊、看完只有更迷惘的看盤仔群組
variations: 盤中閒聊是全台灣最穩定的連續劇：角色固定、台詞固定、結局固定，只有觀眾每天換一批。
我不是沒有立場，我的立場是誰講得比較大聲我就信誰，然後賠給另一邊。

en.content:
My most dependable daily entertainment is the live market thread on the forum.
Bell rings, the bears start chanting: it's rolling over, the slaughter is coming, run.
Night session ticks green and the bulls assemble: it's ripping, no ceiling, hold tight and stop looking.
Same episode every day. Nobody has even bothered to update their lines.
The only thing that changes is me — I believe the bears at open, the bulls by noon, and by the close both camps are right and I'm the one who was a step late in both directions.
en.editorNote: For the group chat that dives into the live market thread every day and comes out more confused than before
variations: The live market thread is the most reliable soap opera in the country: fixed cast, fixed dialogue, fixed ending. Only the audience gets replaced.
It's not that I have no conviction. My conviction is whoever types in the biggest font, and then I pay the other side.

items.sourceNote: 2026 台股一年漲幅接近翻倍、AI 行情主導的討論；改寫原創，寫成「認真選股卻跑輸大盤」的落差（有賺但賺很少，非虧損梗）

zh-tw.content:
這一年大盤幾乎翻了一倍，新聞天天在慶祝。
我也有賺，年報酬百分之五，還是正的，我很滿意。
直到我算了一下：我看了三百天的盤、讀了無數篇分析、換了七次持股。
然後我發現，如果我什麼都不做、什麼都不換，報酬會多好幾倍。
原來我這一年的努力不是白費，它非常有效——有效地把我的報酬砍掉一大半。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個做功課做到半夜、績效卻輸給躺著不動的同事的選股派朋友
variations: 我不是沒賺，我只是用一整年的時間，很努力地買下了跑輸大盤的權利。
最貴的一堂課不是賠錢，是你賺了錢，然後發現什麼都不做的人賺得比你多得多。

en.content:
The index nearly doubled this year. The news celebrated every single day.
I made money too — up five percent, still green, and I was pleased with myself.
Then I did the math: three hundred days of watching charts, countless analyses read, seven rounds of rotating my holdings.
And I realized that if I had done nothing, changed nothing, touched nothing, I'd have made many times more.
So a year of effort wasn't wasted at all. It worked beautifully — it efficiently deleted most of my return.
en.editorNote: For the stock-picking friend who researches until midnight and still loses to the coworker who never touches their account
variations: I didn't lose money. I just spent an entire year working very hard to earn the right to underperform.
The most expensive lesson isn't losing money. It's making money and then finding out the person who did nothing made far more.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 去槓桿效應、台股單日震盪逾 1100 點；改寫原創，寫成手機裡「退休試算」與「維持率查詢」兩個 APP 的切換

zh-tw.content:
我手機裡有兩個常用的頁面。
一個是退休試算，行情好的時候我開它，輸入年齡、輸入金額，看那個數字一直往上長，順便想像自己四十歲住海邊。
另一個是擔保維持率查詢。
這兩個月，我一次都沒打開過退休試算。
人生規劃這種東西很有彈性：行情好的時候是三十年後的藍圖，行情壞的時候是明天早上九點的問題。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個大漲時規劃退休、震盪時只敢看維持率的融資朋友
variations: 我的理財目標會隨行情自動調整：漲的時候是財富自由，跌的時候是不要被追繳。
退休試算跟維持率查詢，是同一支手機裡差最遠的兩個頁面，中間只隔了一根長黑。

en.content:
There are two screens I keep coming back to on my phone.
One is the retirement calculator. When the market's up I open it, punch in my age and my balance, watch the number climb, and picture myself retiring at forty with an ocean view.
The other is the margin maintenance ratio.
I have not opened the retirement calculator once in two months.
Turns out life planning is wonderfully flexible: in a good market it's a thirty-year blueprint, in a bad one it's a problem due at nine tomorrow morning.
en.editorNote: For the leveraged friend who plans retirement on green days and only checks their maintenance ratio on red ones
variations: My financial goals auto-adjust with the market: on the way up it's financial freedom, on the way down it's not getting a margin call.
The retirement calculator and the maintenance ratio screen are the two furthest-apart pages on the same phone, separated by exactly one red candle.

items.sourceNote: 2026「市場最不缺專家、最缺清醒的人」論述，以及多年來一路喊居高思危卻踏空的族群；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
都說市場最不缺專家，最缺的是清醒的人。
我就是那個清醒的人。
指數一萬八，我說太貴了；兩萬八，我說這是泡沫；三萬八，我說遲早要還；四萬八，我還是那句話。
八年下來，我一次都沒錯，我只是一次都沒對。
現在那群不清醒的人陸續買了房，而我保持清醒地，繼續在租。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個從十年前就喊崩盤、至今仍在場邊很有原則地空手的長輩或朋友
variations: 我最擅長的技能是看破泡沫，最不擅長的是活在泡沫破掉之前的那幾年。
清醒的代價，是你會非常準確地看著一件事發生，而且完全沒有參與到。

en.content:
They say the market never runs short of experts — what it lacks is people who stay clear-headed.
That's me. I'm the clear-headed one.
At eighteen thousand I said it was expensive. At twenty-eight thousand, a bubble. At thirty-eight thousand, we'd pay for this eventually. At forty-eight thousand, same line.
Eight years, and I have never once been wrong. I have simply never once been right.
Meanwhile the people who weren't clear-headed have been buying houses, and I am staying admirably clear-headed in my rental.
en.editorNote: For the friend or relative who's been calling the crash for a decade and is still standing on the sidelines, very principled and very flat
variations: My greatest skill is seeing through a bubble. My worst is surviving the years before it pops.
The price of clear-headedness is watching something happen with perfect accuracy and taking absolutely no part in it.

items.sourceNote: 00940 掛牌兩年 486 個交易日僅 28 天站上發行價 10 元、458 天在其下；『幸好募集期間匯款失敗，上市買更便宜』自嘲；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
有一檔 ETF，掛牌兩年、四百多個交易日裡，只有二十幾天站在發行價之上，其他時間全在下面。
我朋友當初想在募集期間就搶進，結果那幾天匯款失敗、沒扣到款。
上市第一天他直接用更便宜的價格買到，逢人就說自己是股神。
我準時繳款的，到現在還在幫他證明：這檔真的很會套人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個抽新股、搶募集，最後套在發行價的定期定額戰友
variations: 理專說發行價十塊很好記，我現在懂了——好記，是因為它從此再也沒回來過。
我這輩子最成功的一次投資，是那次忘記匯款。

en.content:
There's an ETF that, in its first two years and four hundred-odd trading days, spent barely twenty of them above its launch price and all the rest below it.
A friend tried to grab it during the offering, but his transfer failed and the money never went through.
Day one, he bought it cheaper on the open market and has called himself a market genius ever since.
I funded mine on time. To this day I'm just here proving how good this thing is at trapping people.
en.editorNote: For every friend who subscribed to an IPO or fund offering and got stuck right at the launch price
variations: The advisor said a ten-dollar launch price is easy to remember. Now I get it — it's memorable because it never came back.
The single most profitable move of my investing life was the time I forgot to wire the money.

items.sourceNote: 2026 大盤創新高，高股息『低波動』選股在牛市反成低漲幅，存股族看著市值型朋友坐火箭；改寫原創

zh-tw.content:
我買高股息 ETF，看中的就是它低波動、抗跌，跌的時候比較不會痛。
這兩年市場一路衝新高，我朋友的市值型翻了一大截，我的高股息紋風不動。
我才發現，所謂低波動是雙向的：跌的時候抗跌，漲的時候，它也非常抗漲。
它很守信用，不管市場怎麼樣，都堅持讓我原地不動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給每個抱著高股息 ETF、眼睜睜看著市值型朋友坐火箭的存股族
variations: 別人的對帳單在坐雲霄飛車，我的在坐搖搖馬——安全，但也就只是原地搖。
抗跌我信了，抗漲我是真的沒想到還買一送一。

en.content:
I bought a high-dividend ETF for the low volatility — nice and defensive, doesn't hurt as much on the way down.
For two years the market has ripped to new highs, my friend's cap-weighted fund is up a mountain, and mine hasn't moved a hair.
That's when it hit me: low volatility cuts both ways. It resists the drops, and it resists the rallies just as hard.
It's a fund of its word — no matter what the market does, it keeps me exactly where I started.
en.editorNote: For the dividend investor clutching their high-yield ETF while a friend's index fund rides a rocket
variations: Their statement's on a roller coaster. Mine's on a coin-operated pony — safe, and also going nowhere.
I was sold on downside protection. Nobody mentioned it came with free upside protection too.

items.sourceNote: 月配息 ETF 配息一路下修（0.05→0.04→0.03）股東信心崩潰；改寫成『你自己花錢請來的減薪老闆』原創梗

zh-tw.content:
當初我把這檔月配息 ETF 當成一個好老闆，每個月準時發薪水，從不遲到。
這位老闆很特別，減薪的時候完全不用跟我開會、不用公告、也不用給理由。
配息從零點零五，默默變零點零四，再默默變零點零三。
我這才發現，全世界對員工最狠的老闆，是那個你自己花錢請來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個把配息當薪水領、結果被無聲減薪的存股族
variations: 我理想中的被動收入，是躺著領錢；實際上的被動收入，是躺著看它被砍。
別的老闆減薪還會裝作很痛苦，我這個連通知都省了。

en.content:
I used to think of this monthly-dividend ETF as a great boss — pays me on time every month, never late.
Special kind of boss, though: cuts my pay without ever calling a meeting, posting a notice, or giving a reason.
The dividend quietly went from five cents to four, then quietly to three.
That's when I learned the cruelest boss in the world is the one you hired yourself, with your own money.
en.editorNote: For every dividend investor who treated the payout like a paycheck and got a silent pay cut
variations: My dream of passive income was getting paid to lie down. My actual passive income is lying down and watching it get cut.
Other bosses at least fake some regret when they slash your pay. Mine skipped the memo entirely.

items.sourceNote: 月配 ETF 規模從 1750 億縮到 778 億、逾半投資人下車『丟掉』月配；改寫成『沒人記得的演唱會門票』原創梗

zh-tw.content:
這檔月配息 ETF，前年是全民運動，募集的時候大家連夜排隊搶。
規模一度衝到一千七百多億，聚餐時人人都在報自己抱幾張。
兩年後，規模剩不到八百億，一半的人默默下車，同學會再也沒人主動提起它。
我還在，抱著它，像抱著一張沒人記得的演唱會門票——散場了，只剩我還坐在原位。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個當年跟風搶進、如今默默續抱冷門 ETF 的最後一個人
variations: 潮水退了才知道誰沒穿褲子，也才發現當初一起下水的人，早就上岸換好衣服回家了。
它不是被賣掉的，是被大家一個一個悄悄地遺忘的，而我負責記得。

en.content:
Two years ago this monthly-dividend ETF was a national sport — people lined up overnight to grab it at the offering.
The fund ballooned past a hundred and seventy billion, and at every dinner someone was bragging about how many lots they held.
Two years on it's under eighty billion, half the crowd has quietly stepped off, and nobody brings it up at reunions anymore.
I'm still here, holding it like a ticket to a concert no one remembers — the show's over, and I'm the only one still in my seat.
en.editorNote: For the last person still holding the once-hyped ETF everyone else quietly abandoned
variations: When the tide goes out you find out who was swimming naked — and that everyone who jumped in with you already toweled off and went home.
It didn't get sold off. It got quietly forgotten, one holder at a time, and I'm the one on forgetting duty.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 資金明顯從高基期 AI 權值股輪動至中小型題材股（記憶體、邊緣AI、生技）；改寫原創類股輪動 register

zh-tw.content:
大家都說要跟著資金輪動走，於是我認真做功課，追著熱門族群跑。
追到半導體，資金去了記憶體；追到記憶體，資金去了生技；等我追到生技，資金早就回半導體了。
我終於發現自己的天賦——我永遠精準地接到每一段輪動的最後一棒。
別人玩的是類股輪動，我玩的是接力賽，還是那個永遠拿到棒子、卻沒人可以交的最後一棒。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個追著熱門題材跑、卻總是慢半拍的題材追高族
variations: 資金像捷運，每一班我都剛好目送它離站。
我不是不會選股，我只是每次都選在資金準備離開的那一秒。

en.content:
Everyone says to follow the money as it rotates between sectors, so I did my homework and chased whatever was hot.
Chased into chips, the money moved to memory; chased into memory, it moved to biotech; by the time I got to biotech, it had already rotated back to chips.
I finally discovered my superpower: I catch the very last leg of every rotation, every single time.
Others are running a relay of sector rotation. I'm running the same relay, except I'm the guy who always gets handed the baton with no one left to pass it to.
en.editorNote: For the theme-chaser who's always one beat behind the hot money
variations: The money is like a train — every single time, I get there just in time to watch it leave the platform.
It's not that I can't pick stocks. I just always pick them the exact second the money decides to leave.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 報導「只存 0050+0056 資產卻像烏龜爬」；改寫原創龜兔賽跑 register

zh-tw.content:
大家說存市值型 ETF 最穩，像烏龜一樣慢慢爬，總會贏過亂衝的兔子。
於是我乖乖存 0050，安慰自己：慢就是快，穩就是賺。
結果這一年，兔子（飆股）跑到終點放煙火了，我的烏龜還在原地曬太陽。
我才懂，龜兔賽跑的寓言只對了一半——兔子這次沒睡著，是我的烏龜提早退休了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個抱著市值型 ETF、看著飆股絕塵而去的存股族
variations: 別人的兔子在衝刺，我的烏龜在冬眠，同一條跑道，兩種人生。
他們說時間會證明一切，我的烏龜點點頭，然後繼續趴著。

en.content:
They say holding a broad market-cap ETF is the safe play — slow and steady like a tortoise, always beats the reckless hare.
So I dutifully stacked the index fund and told myself: slow is fast, steady is rich.
This year the hare (the momentum names) crossed the line and set off fireworks, while my tortoise is still back at the start, sunbathing.
Turns out the fable is only half right — the hare didn't fall asleep this time. My tortoise just took early retirement.
en.editorNote: For the index-fund holder watching momentum stocks vanish over the horizon
variations: Their hare is sprinting, my tortoise is hibernating — same track, two completely different lives.
They said time would prove everything. My tortoise nodded, then lay back down.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7「大盤跌、飆股飛」格局，資金撤離高基期 AI 權值股轉進中小型題材；改寫原創權值股放生 register

zh-tw.content:
今年很流行一句話：大盤跌，飆股飛。
我聽了很興奮，覺得就算大盤不好，只要抱到飆股就行。
於是我重押了那檔全民最愛的 AI 權值股，想說它最穩最大最不會錯。
結果資金全跑去追中小型題材，我的權值股大到飛不動，只能眼睜睜看著滿天飆股從頭上飛過。
原來『大到不能倒』的下一句，是『大到不會漲』。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給重押大型權值股、卻看著中小型題材股滿天飛的投資人
variations: 我抱的不是龍頭，是壓艙石——穩到動都不會動。
別人的股票在天上飛，我的股票在地上，負責當那片被飛過的天空。

en.content:
There's a popular line this year: the index drops, but the hot stocks fly.
I got excited — even in a bad market, just hold a flyer and you're fine.
So I loaded up on the AI large-cap everyone adored, figuring the biggest and safest name couldn't be wrong.
Then all the money rotated into small-cap themes, and my giant blue chip got too heavy to fly — I just watched a sky full of runners soar right over my head.
Turns out the sequel to 'too big to fail' is 'too big to move.'
en.editorNote: For the investor who went all-in on a mega-cap while the small-cap themes took off without them
variations: What I'm holding isn't a market leader, it's ballast — so stable it doesn't move at all.
Everyone's stock is flying through the sky. Mine is on the ground, playing the role of the sky they fly over.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 建議「主菜市值型＋配菜產業型＋點心高息債」的資產配置說法；改寫原創點餐比喻 register

zh-tw.content:
理財專家教我配置資產，說要像點一頓均衡的餐：主菜配市值型、配菜配產業型、點心來點高息債。
我很聽話，認真點好一整桌。
結果上菜的時候我才發現，主菜是綠的、配菜是綠的、連甜點都綠得發亮。
原來我點的不是均衡餐，是一整桌不同口味的套牢，配色統一，賣相淒涼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給認真做資產配置、卻發現每個部位都在虧的規劃派投資人
variations: 我的投資組合很均衡——均衡地每一檔都在賠。
專家說不要把雞蛋放同一個籃子，我照做了，現在我有好幾個籃子，每個都裝著破掉的蛋。

en.content:
A financial advisor taught me to build a portfolio like ordering a balanced meal: index funds as the main, sector plays as the side, high-yield bonds for dessert.
I followed the recipe and ordered the whole spread.
When the food arrived, the main course was bleeding red, the side was red, and even dessert came out red.
Turns out I didn't order a balanced meal — I ordered a full table of losses in assorted flavors. Coordinated colors, tragic presentation.
en.editorNote: For the diligent asset-allocator who discovered every single position is down
variations: My portfolio is perfectly balanced — balanced so that every single holding is losing money.
They said don't put all your eggs in one basket. I didn't. Now I have several baskets, each holding its own broken egg.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 專家強調「高基期、高波動請謹慎」；改寫原創謹慎反諷 register

zh-tw.content:
今年每個專家都在講同一句話：高基期、高波動，請務必謹慎。
我把『謹慎』兩個字刻在心上，決定嚴守紀律、控管風險。
於是我謹慎地等、謹慎地觀望、謹慎地在指數創新高那天，謹慎地重壓進場。
現在我終於體會什麼叫高基期——我的成本，就是那個最高的基期。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給每個聽完「請謹慎」卻還是買在最高點的投資人
variations: 專家叫我小心追高，我很小心地，追到了最高。
別人的謹慎是等回檔，我的謹慎是確認漲到頂了才敢買。

en.content:
This year every expert repeats the same line: high base, high volatility — please, be cautious.
I carved the word 'cautious' into my heart and vowed to stay disciplined and manage my risk.
So I waited cautiously, watched cautiously, and then, on the very day the index hit an all-time high, I cautiously went all in.
Now I finally understand what 'high base' means — my cost basis is the highest base there is.
en.editorNote: For everyone who heard 'be careful chasing highs' and then bought the exact top
variations: The experts told me to be careful about chasing the top. I was very careful — I chased it all the way to the very top.
Other people's caution means waiting for a pullback. My caution means waiting to confirm it's peaked before I dare to buy.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7/17 台股史上最大單日跌點事件；改寫原創「見證歷史」反諷 register

zh-tw.content:
那天台股寫下史上最大單日跌點，我全程在線，一分一秒都沒錯過。
朋友問我當時在做什麼，我說我在見證歷史。
他問見證的感覺如何，我說——很痛，而且是我出錢讓歷史發生的。
別人買門票進場看展覽，我是自帶本金，親手把自己框進了紀念冊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給在崩盤那天全程盯盤、還自我安慰「至少我見證了歷史」的投資人
variations: 我沒有錯過史上最大跌點——因為那筆跌點裡，有很大一部分是我親自貢獻的。
以後歷史講到這一天，我可以驕傲地說：我在現場，而且我付了全票。

en.content:
That day the market posted its biggest single-day point drop in history, and I was online for every second of it.
A friend asked what I was doing. I said I was witnessing history.
He asked how it felt. I said — it hurt, and I'm the one who paid for history to happen.
Most people buy a ticket to see an exhibit. I brought my own capital and framed myself right into the memorial album.
en.editorNote: For the investor who watched every tick of the crash and consoled themselves with 'at least I witnessed history'
variations: I didn't miss the biggest point drop in history — because a big chunk of that drop was my personal contribution.
When the history books mention this day, I can proudly say: I was there, and I paid full price.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 外媒直擊台股FOMO、散戶借錢喊隨便買；改寫原創牛市股神 register

zh-tw.content:
指數一直創新高，我朋友圈裡每個人都升級成投資大師了。
有人貸款五百萬、有人喊「現在隨便買隨便賺」，講得比法人還篤定。
我問他們風險怎麼辦，他們笑我格局太小。
三週後，當初格局最大的那幾位，現在格局大到要分五年才還得完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給在全民FOMO、人人喊隨便買的高點，還忍住沒有梭哈的清醒散戶
variations: 牛市裡人人都是股神，退潮了才知道誰在裸泳，而且是借錢裸泳。
他說現在隨便買隨便賺，我只信前四個字，後四個字是他自己加的。

en.content:
The index kept hitting new highs, and everyone in my circle suddenly upgraded to investment guru.
One borrowed half a million, another shouted 'just buy anything, you can't lose,' more confident than the institutions.
I asked about risk. They laughed and said my vision was too small.
Three weeks later, the ones with the biggest vision now have a vision so big it takes five years to pay off.
en.editorNote: For the level-headed retail investor who held back from going all-in at the top of a mass-FOMO 'just buy anything' frenzy
variations: In a bull market everyone's a genius; only when the tide goes out do you see who was swimming naked — on borrowed money.
He said just buy anything and you'll profit. I believed the first half. He added the second half himself.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 評論「專家先射箭再畫靶、主升段猜頭」；改寫原創反指標 register

zh-tw.content:
每次大漲，總有專家跳出來說：這裡就是高點，準備回檔。
他們連續喊了半年的頂，指數也很配合地漲了半年。
終於有一天真的跌了，他們立刻發文：看吧，我早就說了。
原來所謂神準，就是先射箭再畫靶——把射歪的那幾百支箭默默撿回來，只留下唯一命中的那一支拍照。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給看膩了「事後諸葛」財經專家、被喊頂喊到麻痺的投資人
variations: 專家不是會猜頭，是猜到天荒地老，總有一次會中。
連續喊頂一百次、中一次就叫神準，這行的容錯率我也想要。

en.content:
Every time the market surges, some expert pops up: this is the top, brace for a pullback.
They called the top for six straight months while the index obligingly climbed for six straight months.
Then one day it finally dropped, and they instantly posted: see, I told you so.
Turns out 'legendary accuracy' just means shooting first and painting the target later — quietly collecting the hundreds of stray arrows and photographing only the one that landed.
en.editorNote: For anyone tired of hindsight-hero market pundits who've called the top so many times it stopped meaning anything
variations: Experts don't predict the top; they predict it forever, so eventually one call has to land.
Call the top a hundred times, get it right once, and they call you a genius. I'd love that error tolerance in my job too.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7 散戶「想賺又害怕」糾結心態；改寫原創克服恐懼買在最高點 register

zh-tw.content:
我這個人最大的問題，就是想賺又害怕。
跌的時候我怕再跌，不敢買；漲的時候我怕買貴，也不敢買。
就這樣糾結了整整一年，終於在某個指數噴到最高的早上，我一時衝動、鼓起這輩子最大的勇氣，克服了恐懼。
事後證明，我這輩子唯一該害怕的，就是我克服恐懼的那一刻。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給長期在「想賺又害怕」之間拉扯、好不容易勇敢一次卻買在最高點的糾結派
variations: 我不是不敢進場，我只是專挑最不該勇敢的那一天勇敢。
膽小一整年幫我躲過了所有下跌，勇敢那一天幫我接住了所有下跌。

en.content:
My biggest problem is that I want to profit but I'm scared.
When it drops I'm scared it'll drop more, so I don't buy. When it rises I'm scared of overpaying, so I don't buy either.
I agonized like this for a whole year, until one morning the index spiked to its peak, and on pure impulse I summoned the greatest courage of my life and conquered my fear.
It later turned out the only thing I should ever have feared was the exact moment I conquered my fear.
en.editorNote: For the perpetually torn investor who finally worked up the nerve — right at the top
variations: It's not that I'm afraid to enter the market; I just specialize in being brave on the one day I shouldn't be.
A whole year of cowardice saved me from every drop. One day of courage caught all of them.

items.sourceNote: 2026 散戶提早卡位AI基礎建設趨勢；改寫原創「早進場 vs 套半山腰」register

zh-tw.content:
我一度很得意，因為我比市場早看到AI基礎建設的趨勢，早早就進場卡位。
朋友都還在觀望，我已經滿手部位，覺得自己是少數清醒的先知。
結果趨勢是對的，股價後來也真的漲了——只是它先帶著我下去半山腰泡了三個月的湯，才慢慢往上爬。
原來「早進場」和「套在半山腰」，中間只差一句自我安慰。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給看對長線AI趨勢、卻因為進場太早先被套一輪的「先知型」散戶
variations: 我不是買錯方向，我只是買在對的方向裡最貴的那一段。
先知的痛苦在於：你看對了趨勢，卻要先替趨勢繳完學費。

en.content:
I was so proud — I spotted the AI infrastructure trend before the market and got in early to stake my claim.
While friends were still watching, I was already fully positioned, feeling like one of the few clear-eyed prophets.
The trend was right and the price did eventually climb — it just took me down to soak halfway up the mountain for three months first, then slowly crawled back up.
Turns out 'getting in early' and 'stuck halfway up the mountain' are separated by nothing but a line of self-consolation.
en.editorNote: For the 'prophet' retail investor who called the long-term AI trend right but got buried for entering too early
variations: I didn't buy the wrong direction; I just bought the most expensive stretch of the right direction.
The pain of being a prophet: you're right about the trend, but you pay its tuition first.

items.sourceNote: 行為財務學「心理帳戶」：散戶把獲利當意外之財花掉、虧損卻算進本金，導致本金越滾越小。原創改寫成自嘲段子。

zh-tw.content:
我腦袋裡有兩個帳戶。
賺到的那筆叫「天上掉下來的」，當天就變成火鍋、耳機跟一趟小旅行。
賠掉的那筆叫「本來就是我的」，會很有耐心地從本金裡慢慢扣。
這套會計制度運作三年，結論非常穩定：快樂都花完了，虧損全部留著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合曬完戰績隔天又默默補錢進帳戶的人，或想吐槽自己「賺就花、賠就扛」的雙標記帳法
variations: 我的獲利有腳，會自己跑去買東西；我的虧損有根，會住在帳戶裡。
我不是沒賺過，是賺到的都變成照片，賠掉的都變成餘額。
原來所謂「本金越做越小」，不是市場拿走的，是我自己請客請掉的。

en.content:
There are two accounts in my head.
The money I make is filed under "free money from the sky" and becomes dinner, headphones, and a weekend trip by nightfall.
The money I lose is filed under "that was always mine anyway" and gets deducted from the principal very patiently.
Three years of running this accounting system, and the results are remarkably consistent: the fun is all spent, the losses are all still here.
en.editorNote: For anyone who celebrates a green day out loud and quietly wires more cash in the next morning
variations: My gains have legs and walk off to buy things. My losses have roots and live in the account.
It's not that I never made money — it's that the wins became photos and the losses became my balance.
Turns out my shrinking principal wasn't taken by the market. I picked up the check myself.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年散戶普遍改用 AI 助理問盤勢；原創改寫成「求許可而不是求建議」的心理段子。

zh-tw.content:
套牢之後，我開始問 AI。
它很有良心，每次都先告訴我它不能給投資建議，然後叫我想想自己的風險承受度。
我不死心，換個問法再問一次，再換一個角度再問一次，問到第七次，它終於講出一句聽起來像在支持我的話。
我馬上截圖存起來。
後來我才承認：我從頭到尾要的都不是分析，是有人願意陪我一起裝作沒事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給已經問遍所有 AI 跟朋友、只為了找一個人點頭的套牢族
variations: 我不是在做研究，我是在找一個願意跟我說「應該還好」的對象。
問到第七次才滿意，代表我要的答案，前六次它都誠實地講了。
AI 很難不給我建議，因為我會一直改題目，直到它不小心說中我想聽的。

en.content:
After I got stuck, I started asking the AI.
It's very responsible — every time it reminds me it can't give investment advice and asks me to think about my own risk tolerance.
So I rephrase. Then rephrase again. On the seventh try, it finally says something that sounds vaguely like it's on my side.
I screenshot that one immediately.
Eventually I admitted it: I was never looking for analysis. I was looking for someone willing to pretend with me that everything is fine.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has interrogated every chatbot and group chat just to get one person to nod
variations: I wasn't doing research. I was auditioning someone to tell me "it's probably fine."
If it took seven tries to get the answer I liked, the first six were the honest ones.
It's hard for a chatbot to refuse me advice when I'll keep rewriting the question until it slips.

items.sourceNote: 大跌後散戶自我安慰的觀看行為；原創改寫成「拉長線圖週期來美化心情」的段子。

zh-tw.content:
大跌那天，我打開線圖，日線醜到我不敢直視。
沒關係，我切到週線，還是很醜。
切到月線，勉強有個形狀。
切到年線，看起來居然還在往上。
我最後切到「上市以來」，畫面終於一片欣欣向榮。
原來療癒不用花錢，把時間拉長就好——我只是得假裝這幾年不存在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合大跌隔天、只敢看長週期線圖的人，或想吐槽自己「看不順眼就換尺度」
variations: 我的心情好壞，取決於我把時間軸拉多長。
日線看不下去就看月線，月線看不下去就看人生——反正總有一個角度是漲的。
所謂長期投資者，就是把線圖縮到自己看起來還沒輸的那個倍率。

en.content:
On the big red day I opened the chart. The daily view was too ugly to look at.
Fine — switch to weekly. Still ugly.
Monthly. Okay, there's a shape now.
Yearly. Somehow it's going up.
I finally zoomed all the way out to "since listing," and the screen looked positively glorious.
Turns out therapy is free. You just stretch the time axis and pretend the last few years didn't happen.
en.editorNote: For the day after a selloff, when the only chart you can face is the zoomed-out one
variations: My mood depends entirely on how far I zoom out.
Can't stand the daily? Try monthly. Can't stand monthly? Try your whole life. Some scale is always green.
A long-term investor is just someone who found the zoom level where they haven't lost yet.

items.sourceNote: 心理帳戶/分類效應延伸：投資人用重新歸類的方式緩解虧損痛感。原創改寫成券商 APP 自選群組的段子。

zh-tw.content:
券商 APP 可以自己開自選群組，我開了三個。
第一個叫「觀察中」，第二個叫「短線」，第三個叫「長期持有」。
這三個群組唯一的規則是：只要一檔股票賠超過兩成，它就會自動被我調去「長期持有」。
所以我的「長期持有」名單越來越長，而且每一檔都是被貶職進去的。
我沒有改變任何持股，我只是幫它們改了名字，然後心情就好多了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給用資料夾分類治療虧損的人，或想吐槽自己「賠到一個程度就自動改叫長期投資」
variations: 我的長期投資，全部都是短線失敗之後升格的。
改變不了股價，至少我改得動分類。
「長期持有」在我的 APP 裡不是策略，是一個收容所。

en.content:
My brokerage app lets me make custom watchlists, so I made three.
One is "Watching," one is "Short-term," and one is "Long-term Holds."
There's exactly one rule governing them: the moment a position is down more than twenty percent, it gets quietly moved into "Long-term Holds."
So that list keeps getting longer, and every name on it was demoted there.
I didn't change a single position. I just renamed the folder, and I felt much better.
en.editorNote: For anyone treating their losses with folder management instead of decisions
variations: Every long-term hold I own was promoted there by failing as a short-term trade.
I can't move the price, but I can definitely move the label.
In my app, "long-term" isn't a strategy. It's a shelter.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年多家上市櫃公司公告減資彌補虧損（減資比例約 16～18%，屬帳面調整、不退還現金）的市場現象；原創改寫成散戶視角段子，非個股評論。

zh-tw.content:
我那檔套了兩年的股票，公司終於發公告了：辦理減資，彌補虧損，改善財務結構。
我以為終於有人要來救我了，結果點開細節——股數銷掉快兩成，剩下的股票價格等比例往上調。
張數變少了，成本變高了，虧損金額一毛都沒變。
公司說這叫體質改善，我覺得比較像我客人來訪前的整理房間：東西一樣都沒丟，只是排得比較整齊，看起來比較不像案發現場。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合手上持股宣布減資彌補虧損時發，或想吐槽「純屬帳面調整」這幾個字
variations: 減資不會讓我少賠，只會讓我的虧損重新排版一次。
公司改善財務結構的方式，是先把我的股數改善掉一部分。

en.content:
That position I've been stuck in for two years finally sent me a notice: capital reduction, to clear accumulated losses and improve the balance sheet.
For one beautiful second I thought somebody was coming to rescue me. Then I read the details. Almost a fifth of the shares get cancelled, and the survivors get their price adjusted up to match.
Fewer shares. Higher cost basis. Loss identical to the dollar.
The company calls this a healthier structure. I call it what I do to my apartment before guests arrive: nothing actually left the building, it's just arranged so it looks less like a crime scene.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose stuck position just announced a "purely accounting" capital reduction
variations: A capital reduction didn't shrink my loss. It reformatted it.
They improved the balance sheet by removing part of my shares from it.

items.sourceNote: 2026/7/29 台股處置股增至 29 檔、部分改採 5 分鐘或 20 分鐘分盤交易並限制單筆委託張數的新聞背景；原創改寫，不指涉任何個股。

zh-tw.content:
我追的那檔漲太兇，被列進處置名單，改成五分鐘撮合一次，一筆最多只能下十張。
交易所說，這是為了保護投資人。
結果它真的有效：我從每三秒刷新一次，變成五分鐘才能知道結果，連部位大小都被強制縮小。
我這輩子唯一成功執行的資金控管，不是我自己做到的，是被別人把手綁住才做到的。
現在我不看股價了，我看那個倒數計時。焦慮沒有變少，只是被排進了時間表。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合手上有股票被列處置、被迫五分鐘撮合的時候發，也適合吐槽自己的自制力得靠外力
variations: 原來我需要的從來不是紀律，是有人幫我把下單按鈕鎖起來。
五分鐘撮合一次，我的心跳也跟著改成五分鐘結算一次。

en.content:
The name I chased ran so hard the exchange dropped it onto the disposition list: matching once every five minutes, ten lots max per order.
The exchange says this is to protect investors.
And it worked. I went from refreshing every three seconds to learning where I stand every five minutes, with my position size capped whether I liked it or not.
The only successful risk management of my entire investing life wasn't something I did. It happened because somebody tied my hands.
Now I don't watch the price. I watch the countdown. The anxiety didn't shrink. It just got put on a schedule.
en.editorNote: For the day a position gets throttled into batch matching, or for anyone whose self-control only works when it's enforced
variations: Turns out I never needed discipline. I needed someone to take the buy button away.
Matching every five minutes just means I now panic every five minutes, punctually.

items.sourceNote: 台灣現行制度：股利所得須申報課稅，證券交易所得停徵、虧損無從扣抵，賣出時另課證券交易稅。以此制度落差為梗的原創改寫，非稅務或投資建議。

zh-tw.content:
報稅那天，我很認真地把去年整理出來。
虧損那一欄：一個很難念出口的數字，而系統上沒有任何地方可以填它。
股利那一欄：兩萬多，系統早就幫我抓好了，一毛都沒漏。
我打電話去問，對方很客氣：股利是所得，虧損是您自己的事。
原來我跟這個市場的關係一直很清楚——賺的部分大家一起算，賠的部分我自己收好。
連我含淚按下賣出的那一秒，都還要順手繳一筆證交稅，當作出場費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合五月報稅季，或每次認賠賣出、在成交明細裡看到那行稅金的時候發
variations: 我的虧損沒有人承認，只有我自己記得。
領息是公開資訊，賠錢是個人興趣，這個市場分得很乾淨。

en.content:
Filing day. I sat down and honestly put last year together.
The losses: a number I can't say out loud, and no box on the form that wants to hear it.
The dividends: a couple thousand, already filled in for me, down to the cent.
I called to ask about it. The person on the line explained it very politely: dividends are income, losses are a personal matter.
So my relationship with this market has always been clear. The upside we tally together. The downside I take home in a bag.
And on the day I finally cried and hit sell, I still paid a transaction tax on the way out, like a cover charge for leaving.
en.editorNote: For filing season, or the moment you spot the tax line on a losing sale
variations: Nobody recognizes my losses. I'm the only one keeping the records.
Gains go on the form. Losses are just a hobby I fund myself.

items.sourceNote: 七、八月除權息旺季；「填息 vs 貼息」制度常識為梗的原創改寫，非投資建議、不指涉個股

zh-tw.content:
除權息旺季到了，股利入帳那天我特地截圖，覺得自己終於是個有被動收入的人。
然後我打開線圖：除息當天，股價先把那筆錢原封不動扣了回去，接下來三個月都躺在那條線下面。
所謂填息，就是市場慢慢把我自己的錢還給我，還要我等，而且不保證還得完。
我不是在領股利，我是借了一筆錢給自己，利息還沒談好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在股利入帳那天，配一張還在貼息的線圖發限動
variations: 我的股利很準時，股價把它扣回去也一樣準時。
填息是一種信仰，貼息才是日常作息。

en.content:
Dividend season came around. The cash hit my account and I screenshotted it like proof that I have passive income.
Then I opened the chart. On the ex-date the price got docked by exactly that amount, and it's been lying under that line for three months.
So closing the dividend gap just means the market hands me back my own money, slowly, with no promise it'll finish.
I didn't collect a dividend. I loaned myself some cash and forgot to set the terms.
en.editorNote: Post it the day your dividend lands, next to a chart still sitting below the ex-date gap
variations: My dividend arrives on schedule. So does the price cut that takes it straight back.
Closing the gap is a belief system. Sitting under it is the daily routine.

items.sourceNote: 股板常見「看盤看到血壓高」register；健檢紅字 vs 對帳單顏色的對照為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
年度健檢報告拿到手，紅字三行：血壓偏高、睡眠不足、壓力過大。
醫生說，紅字當然是越少越好。
我心裡想，這句話在我每天看的另一個畫面剛好相反，那邊的紅字是越多越好。
一年下來我很努力地兩邊兼顧，成果是——健檢紅字多了兩行，對帳單綠得非常整齊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合健檢報告跟對帳單同一週寄到的時候，發給一起看盤的同事
variations: 醫生要我遠離壓力來源，我點頭答應，然後打開看盤軟體。
我的血壓跟指數是同步的，差別在於指數還會回檔。

en.content:
Annual physical came back with three lines flagged in red: blood pressure high, sleep too short, stress elevated.
The doctor said the goal is obviously fewer red lines.
Funny thing — in the other screen I stare at every day, the goal is more green ones.
A year of effort later, I've achieved both: two more red lines on the report, and a beautifully consistent wall of red in the portfolio.
en.editorNote: For the week your checkup results and your brokerage statement arrive together — send it to whoever watches the market next to you
variations: My doctor told me to stay away from my source of stress. I nodded, then opened the trading app.
My blood pressure tracks the index perfectly. The difference is the index actually pulls back sometimes.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 財經節目常見「八月先蹲後跳」說法；改寫為原創自嘲，不涉及漲跌預測或個股

zh-tw.content:
電視上的老師說，這波行情是先蹲後跳，蹲完自然就會往上。
我聽了很安心，決定跟著蹲。
第一週蹲、第二週蹲、第三週我還蹲在原地。
現在我不確定的已經不是它會不會跳，而是我的腳麻到站不太起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在名嘴喊「整理完就會漲」、你卻越等越深的時候，丟給一起在等的朋友
variations: 所有的先蹲後跳，最後跳起來的都是別人。
蹲太久的問題不是腳麻，是你會開始說服自己這叫坐著。

en.content:
The guy on the finance channel said this stretch would crouch first and then jump — a little consolidation, then up we go.
That sounded reassuring, so I crouched right along with it.
Week one, crouching. Week two, crouching. Week three, same exact position.
At this point what I'm unsure about isn't whether it jumps. It's whether my legs still work.
en.editorNote: For when the talking heads keep saying 'after this consolidation,' and you're the one still waiting — send it to whoever's waiting with you
variations: Every 'it'll bounce after this' I ever believed bounced without me in it.
The problem with waiting too long isn't the numbness. It's that you start calling it a strategy.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 市場「一邊腰斬、一邊狂噴」分化評論；改寫為原創自嘲，不指涉任何個股

zh-tw.content:
有人幫這個月的行情下了註解：一邊腰斬，一邊狂噴。
我看完覺得寫得真準，因為這兩邊我都有參與。
狂噴的那一區，我在起漲前三天嫌它太貴，賣了。
腰斬的那一區，我在最後一根長紅覺得它終於便宜，加碼了。
同一個月、兩種行情，我用一個人的資金，精準地站錯了兩次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合月底檢討持股、發現兩種行情自己都沒賺到的時候發
variations: 別人是選錯股，我是連續選錯兩次，效率高很多。
行情分化的時候我很公平，兩邊的虧我都領。

en.content:
Someone summed up the month in one line: half the market got cut in half, the other half went vertical.
Great description, because I managed to be in both halves.
The vertical half — I decided it was too expensive three days before it ran, and sold.
The half that got cut down — I decided it finally looked cheap on the last big green candle, and added.
One month, two markets, one guy's money, wrong side twice.
en.editorNote: For the end-of-month portfolio review where you realize neither half of the market paid you
variations: Other people pick the wrong stock. I picked the wrong side twice, which is much more efficient.
When the market splits in two, I stay perfectly fair about it and collect the loss from both sides.

items.sourceNote: 股板「本來要買 XX，結果錢拿去加碼」機會成本 register；改寫原創，不指涉個股

zh-tw.content:
我的手機用了五年，螢幕裂了一角，早就該換。
算一算換一支要三萬多，我捨不得，決定先把這筆錢拿去加碼那檔「很有機會」的，賺到再換。
三個月後，那筆錢剩下不到一半。
所以現在我不但沒有新手機，還得用這支裂角的舊手機，每天打開軟體，看它慢慢變得更少。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合滑到新機發表會的新聞、又剛好點開自己庫存的時候自嘲
variations: 我把消費降級了，沒想到投資跟著一起降級。
省下來的錢沒有變成新手機，變成了一堂學費。

en.content:
My phone is five years old with a cracked corner and should have been replaced ages ago.
A new one runs about a thousand bucks. I couldn't bring myself to spend it, so I put the money into something with 'a lot of upside' and figured I'd buy the phone out of the gains.
Three months later that money is worth less than half.
So now I don't have a new phone, and I get to open the app on the same cracked screen every day and watch the number get smaller.
en.editorNote: For scrolling past a launch-event headline right after checking your own positions
variations: I downgraded my spending. Somehow my investing downgraded along with it.
The money I saved never turned into a phone. It turned into tuition.

items.sourceNote: 定期定額扣款機制與台股定期定額金額成長報導；改寫為原創情境，不指涉個股、不構成建議

zh-tw.content:
上個月我發完畢業文，刪掉券商 APP、清空自選股，跟所有人宣布我退出了。
唯一忘記處理的，是那筆每月六號自動扣三千的定期定額。
三個月後我忍不住重新登入，發現整個帳戶裡唯一還在慢慢變多的，就是那筆我忘記取消的。
原來我這輩子最像樣的一次操作，是我全程沒有參與的那一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合朋友問你「不是說不玩了嗎」的時候，用來自嘲兼解釋
variations: 我的紀律不是自律，是我懶得去按取消。
我最好的投資顧問，是我的健忘。

en.content:
Last month I posted my goodbye note, deleted the broker app, wiped my watchlist, and told everyone I was done.
The one thing I forgot to deal with was the auto-transfer that pulls a hundred bucks out on the sixth of every month.
Three months later I caved and logged back in. The only thing in the account that had quietly gotten bigger was the thing I forgot to cancel.
Turns out the best move I ever made was the one I wasn't there for.
en.editorNote: For when a friend asks why you're back after swearing you quit
variations: My discipline isn't discipline. It's laziness attached to a direct debit.
My best financial advisor is my own forgetfulness.

items.sourceNote: 盤中零股交易擬改為九點與整股同步開盤、最快 2026 年底上路；改寫為原創自嘲情境

zh-tw.content:
新聞說盤中零股要改成九點跟整股同步開盤了，留言區一片歡呼，說小資族的春天終於來了。
只有我看完有點慌。
以前零股慢半拍，我衝動下單之後，還有一小段時間可以後悔、可以刪單、可以假裝剛剛那個不是我。
現在連那段時間都要沒了——我的衝動，正式升級成即時到帳。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看到交易制度更新的新聞、心裡想的卻是自己手速的時候
variations: 制度越來越方便，我的自制力越來越沒有藉口。
以前我輸給行情，以後我要輸得更即時一點。

en.content:
The exchange is moving odd-lot trading to open at nine, in sync with the regular session. The comments are all cheering that small investors finally get a fair shake.
I'm the only one who read it and got nervous.
Odd lots used to run on a delay, which meant that after every impulsive order I still had a small window to regret it, cancel it, and pretend that wasn't me.
That window is going away. My impulses have officially been upgraded to real time.
en.editorNote: For reading a market-rules update and immediately thinking about your own trigger finger
variations: Every upgrade to the system takes away one more excuse for my lack of self-control.
I used to lose to the market. Soon I'll get to lose with zero latency.

items.sourceNote: 月初市場展望報導（名師看 8 月台股區間、築底震盪）；改寫為原創情境，不預測價格、不指涉個股

zh-tw.content:
月初的專家專訪：這個月大概就是區間震盪，築底之後再看。
我看完覺得很有道理，還認真抄在筆記本上。
月底回頭對照，指數確實乖乖待在那個區間裡，專家全中。
只有我不在區間裡——我在上緣追進去、在下緣砍出來，硬是把一個「震盪」走成了「虧損」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看完月度行情展望、又剛好打開自己對帳單的那個瞬間
variations: 區間開得夠寬，預測就永遠不會錯。
指數在區間裡震盪，我在區間裡反覆受傷。

en.content:
Start of the month, the expert roundup: expect a range, choppy, wait for a base to form.
Sounded very reasonable. I even wrote it down.
End of the month, the index had indeed stayed politely inside that range. The experts nailed it.
I was the one outside it. I chased at the top of the range and bailed at the bottom, and personally turned 'choppy' into 'down.'
en.editorNote: For finishing a monthly outlook piece and then opening your own statement
variations: Make the range wide enough and the forecast can never be wrong.
The index went sideways. I went down. Same month, different chart.

items.sourceNote: 全民瘋股市與投資人心理健康報導；改寫為原創自嘲情境

zh-tw.content:
手機每個禮拜一早上都會很盡責地丟給我一份螢幕使用時間報告。
這週：平均每天七小時二十分，比上週多了四成一。
使用時間第一名，券商 APP。
第二名，計算機——因為我每天都要重算一次，還差多少才回得了本。
第三名，相簿。我在翻那張還有賺錢的截圖。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合週一早上被自己手機打臉的時候發
variations: 我的螢幕使用時間，忠實記錄了我不肯放手的全過程。
別人用這份報告檢討生活，我用它確認自己還在原地。

en.content:
Every Monday morning my phone dutifully hands me a screen-time report.
This week: seven hours twenty a day, up forty-one percent.
Most-used app: my broker.
Second: the calculator, because I recompute how far I am from break-even at least once a day.
Third: photos, where I keep going back to the screenshot from when I was still up.
en.editorNote: For getting called out by your own phone first thing Monday morning
variations: My screen-time report is just a detailed log of me refusing to let go.
Most people use that report to fix their week. I use it to confirm I haven't moved.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 台股去槓桿、融資餘額減幅超過大盤修正幅度的市場評論；改寫為原創自嘲，不指涉個股、不預測漲跌

zh-tw.content:
分析師在節目上說，這一波把浮額洗得很乾淨，市場體質變健康了，是好事。
我卡在「洗得很乾淨」那五個字上。
因為我就是被洗掉的那一批：融資被追繳、部位縮到剩零頭、名字從所有統計裡安靜地消失。
市場確實變健康了，代價是把我洗出去。
我現在也很乾淨，乾淨到什麼都不剩。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看到「籌碼沉澱、體質轉健康」這類評論、自己卻剛認賠出場的時候
variations: 市場的體質，是靠洗掉我這種人養好的。
他們口中的浮額，有名有姓，就是我。

en.content:
The analyst on TV said this stretch washed out the weak hands, the market's structurally healthier now, and that's a good thing.
I got stuck on 'washed out.'
Because that's me. Margin called, position shrunk to a rounding error, name quietly deleted from every statistic.
The market really is healthier. The price of that was me.
I'm very clean now too. Clean as in there's nothing left.
en.editorNote: For hearing 'the weak hands are flushed out' the same week you closed everything at a loss
variations: The market gets healthier by removing people like me.
When they say weak hands, they mean mine specifically.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 台股總開戶人數再創新高的報導；改寫為原創情境，不引用具體數字、不指涉個股

zh-tw.content:
新聞說全台開戶人數又創新高的那天，我算了一下，那裡面有三戶是我的。
對外的說法是：手續費要比較，下單要分散。
真正的原因是，同一筆虧損拆進三個 APP 之後，每一個打開來都還在可以接受的範圍。
上禮拜我不小心把三張對帳單並排看。
數字沒有變多，我只是終於聽懂它們一直在講同一件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你準備開第四個帳戶之前，先傳給自己看一次
variations: 我沒有分散風險，我只是分散了會看到風險的地方。
帳戶可以開很多個，本金從頭到尾只有一份。

en.content:
The day the country set another record for brokerage accounts opened, I did the math: three of them are mine.
The official reason is comparing fees and spreading out my orders.
The real reason is that one loss split across three apps looks completely survivable in each one.
Last week I accidentally lined all three statements up side by side.
The number didn't get bigger. I just finally understood they'd been saying the same thing all along.
en.editorNote: For the moment right before you open a fourth account
variations: I didn't diversify my risk. I diversified where I have to look at it.
You can open as many accounts as you want. There's still only one pile of money.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 證交所處置股新制（關禁閉天數縮短、撮合頻率加快，8/10 上路）與「流動性殺手」輿論；改寫為原創自嘲，不指涉個股

zh-tw.content:
新聞說交易所要放寬處置股的限制了，理由是原本那套規定根本是流動性殺手。
留言區一片歡呼，說終於還我流動性。
我看了看自己的庫存：三檔套了兩年，每天開盤都可以自由買賣，我一張也沒動過。
真正殺掉我流動性的從來不是制度。
是那句「等它回到我的成本價，我就走」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看到交易制度鬆綁的新聞、心裡浮出的卻是自己那幾檔動不了的持股
variations: 我的資金沒有被關禁閉，是我自己不肯放它出來。
制度可以改，我那句「再等一下」不行。

en.content:
The exchange is loosening the restrictions it slaps on overheated stocks. The stated reason: the old rules were a liquidity killer.
The comments are all cheering about finally getting their liquidity back.
Then there's my account. Three positions, underwater for two years, freely tradable every single session, and I haven't touched one of them.
Nothing in the rulebook killed my liquidity.
It was the sentence 'I'll sell the moment it gets back to my cost.'
en.editorNote: For reading a rule-change headline while sitting on three things you refuse to sell
variations: My money isn't locked up by the exchange. I'm the one who won't let it out.
They can change the rules. They can't change my 'just a little longer.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 散戶情緒交易調查（自認情緒投資人比例遠低於實際情緒下單比例）；改寫為原創情境，不引用具體數字

zh-tw.content:
券商寄了一份風險屬性問卷過來，我很認真地填。
「您是否會因為情緒改變投資決策？」我勾了否。
「您能否承受本金大幅波動？」我勾了可以。
結果出來：積極型，跟我想的一模一樣。
那天下午我看到一根長紅就衝了進去，晚上翻來覆去睡不著，隔天開盤第一分鐘砍掉。
我對自己的判斷完全正確——那份問卷唯一沒問的，是我做不做得到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛填完風險屬性問卷、同一週就被自己打臉的時候
variations: 我很了解自己，只是了解跟做得到是兩回事。
問卷測的是我想成為的那個人，市場測的是我本人。

en.content:
My broker sent over a risk-profile questionnaire and I filled it out honestly.
'Do your emotions influence your investment decisions?' No.
'Can you tolerate large swings in your principal?' Yes.
Result: aggressive investor. Exactly what I'd have guessed.
That afternoon I chased a big green candle, lay awake all night, and cut it in the first minute of the next open.
My self-assessment was completely accurate. The questionnaire just never asked whether I could actually do any of it.
en.editorNote: For the week your risk questionnaire and your actual behavior openly disagree
variations: I know myself very well. Knowing and doing are sold separately.
The questionnaire measures who I'd like to be. The market measures who I am.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 台股單月出現十四個盤中高低差逾千點的交易日、創史上最大單日漲點與第三大跌點；改寫為原創的情緒鈍化自嘲，不預測方向

zh-tw.content:
七月那一個月，盤中高低差超過一千點的日子多到我懶得數。
剛開始每跳一下，我的心臟就跟著跳一下。到後來，我看到負三百點的第一個念頭是：今天好平靜，可以去吃個飯。
朋友說你最近變得好穩，這就是經驗吧。
我點頭，但我心裡很清楚——我不是變穩，是刻度壞了。
以前跌三百點是一件事，現在它得跌到我睡不著，我才願意承認今天有事發生。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合經歷完一整個月的劇烈震盪、才發現自己對數字已經沒感覺的時候
variations: 我不是抗壓性變好，是感覺神經先陣亡了。
以前三百點是一場災難，現在它只是背景音。

en.content:
For one whole month, sessions that swung more than a thousand points intraday were so routine I stopped counting them.
At first every tick moved my pulse. By the end, I'd see the index down three hundred and think: nice and quiet today, maybe I'll go get lunch.
A friend told me I've gotten so steady lately, that's what experience does.
I nodded. But I know what actually happened. I didn't get steadier. My scale broke.
Three hundred points used to be an event. Now it has to keep me up at night before I'll admit anything happened at all.
en.editorNote: For when a month of violent swings has left you feeling nothing at all
variations: I didn't build tolerance. My nerve endings just clocked out first.
Three hundred points used to be a disaster. Now it's background noise.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 網路上原型 ETF 與兩倍槓桿型 ETF 是否適合長期持有的論戰；改寫為原創的言行落差自嘲，不指涉任何代號、不做推薦

zh-tw.content:
某篇文章底下又吵起來了：到底該抱原型的，還是那種兩倍槓桿的。
我寫了一段很長的留言，講波動耗損、講你有沒有真的算過自己的承受度、講你撐不撐得過一次腰斬。語氣冷靜又誠懇。
那則留言拿到整串最多讚，還有人回我：受教了。
然後我切回自己的帳戶，看著佔比最高的那一檔。
原來我是很懂投資的，只是我的理性有指定用途——專門發給別人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛在網路上勸完別人穩健、回頭打開自己庫存卻笑不出來的時候
variations: 我最理性的部位，永遠是別人的部位。
我不是嘴上一套心裡一套，我是嘴上一套、帳戶一套。

en.content:
Another comment war broke out over whether you should hold the plain index fund or the two-times leveraged version of it.
I wrote a long, calm reply about volatility decay, about whether anyone had honestly measured their own tolerance, about whether you could really sit still while your money got cut in half.
It got the most likes in the thread. Someone replied that they'd learned something.
Then I switched back to my own account and looked at my single largest position.
So I do understand investing. My good judgment just comes with a label on it: for external use only.
en.editorNote: For the moment you finish preaching prudence online and then open your own holdings
variations: My most rational portfolio is always somebody else's.
It's not that I say one thing and think another. I say one thing and hold another.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 各券商晨訊投資建議摘要（同一天多家看法互相矛盾）；改寫為原創的確認偏誤自嘲，不引用任何具體建議或標的

zh-tw.content:
我每天早上八點準時讀完各家券商的晨間報告，一篇都不漏。
八家有八種說法：有的說拉回就是機會，有的說在這個位置要特別留意，還有一家很厲害，同一段裡兩句都寫了。
我讀得很認真，讀到第三十分鐘，終於找到一句跟我昨天晚上就打定的主意同一個方向。
我把那句話截下來，心情踏實地下了單。
很久以後我才願意承認：我不是在做功課，我是在找一個願意幫我簽名的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合發現自己讀報告不是為了做決定、而是為了幫衝動找背書的時候
variations: 八份報告我只挑走一句，而那句我開盤前就寫好了。
我讀的不是研究報告，是同意書。

en.content:
Every morning at eight I read all the brokerage morning notes. Every single one.
Eight firms, eight opinions. Pullbacks are opportunities. Be careful up at these levels. One of them impressively managed both in the same paragraph.
I read carefully, and about thirty minutes in I finally found one sentence pointing the same way as the decision I'd already made the night before.
I screenshotted that sentence and placed my order feeling thoroughly researched.
It took me a long time to admit it: I wasn't doing homework. I was looking for someone willing to co-sign.
en.editorNote: For realizing your research exists to rubber-stamp a decision you already made
variations: I pulled one line out of eight reports, and I'd written that line before the open.
That's not research. That's a permission slip.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 台股高檔劇烈震盪、投資人重新檢視持股的市場氛圍；改寫為原創的錨定效應自嘲，不提任何價位預測

zh-tw.content:
上個月某天盤中，我的帳戶出現過一個很漂亮的數字。
它存在大概四十分鐘。我沒有按下賣出，因為我覺得它應該還會更漂亮。
它沒有。
奇怪的是，從那天以後，我心裡的本金就悄悄換成了那個數字。
現在每天收盤，我算的不是我賠了多少，是我離那四十分鐘還差多少。
那筆錢我從來沒有真的拿到過，但我已經很認真地，為它難過了一整個月。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合心裡的成本價早就換成帳戶曾經閃過的最高數字、怎麼算都覺得虧的時候
variations: 那個數字只出現過四十分鐘，卻負責幫我記帳一整個月。
我不是在算虧損，我是在算一個從來沒到手的東西。

en.content:
One session last month, my account showed a very beautiful number.
It lasted about forty minutes. I didn't hit sell, because I figured it was going to get prettier.
It did not.
The strange part is that ever since, that number quietly became my baseline.
Now at every close I'm not calculating what I lost. I'm calculating how far I am from those forty minutes.
I never actually had that money. I've just been sincerely grieving it for a month.
en.editorNote: For when your mental cost basis quietly became the highest number your account ever flashed
variations: That number existed for forty minutes and has been doing my accounting ever since.
I'm not measuring a loss. I'm measuring the distance to something I never held.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年券商大力推廣「閒置持股出借賺利息」的存股族第二筆收入概念；改寫為原創的自嘲，不涉及任何個股或操作建議

zh-tw.content:
券商推播說：您的閒置持股可以出借，讓資產自己去工作。
我那檔套兩年的，本來就閒置到快長香菇，反正我也捨不得賣，出借賺點利息好像很划算。
借出去的第三天，它開始一路往下。
我後來才弄懂一件事：會想跟我借這檔的人，看到的東西跟我看到的不一樣。
我收到的利息，一天不到一杯飲料。
所以我不只是被套牢，我還很有禮貌地把武器遞給對方，順便說了聲謝謝惠顧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合把套牢股拿去出借賺利息、才發現借走的人比自己更懂這檔的時候
variations: 這不叫資產活化，這叫自備武器。
利息一天不到一杯飲料，代價是後面整段下坡。

en.content:
My broker pushed a notification: your idle shares can be lent out, let your assets work for you.
The one I'd been stuck in for two years was already idle enough to grow mushrooms, and I couldn't bring myself to sell it anyway, so earning a little interest sounded like a great deal.
Three days after I lent it out, it started sliding.
It took me a while to work out that whoever wanted to borrow it was looking at something I wasn't.
The interest comes to less than a cup of coffee a day.
So I'm not just stuck. I politely handed someone the weapon, and thanked them for their business.
en.editorNote: For when you lend out the position you're trapped in and realize the borrower reads it better than you do
variations: This isn't putting my assets to work. This is supplying the ammunition.
Less than a cup of coffee a day in interest, in exchange for the entire way down.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 定期定額存股與親子帳戶「教育基金」的普遍理財敘事；改寫為原創的親子自嘲，不提個股、不給建議

zh-tw.content:
我幫小孩開了一個帳戶，說是教育基金，順便讓他從小認識複利的力量。
開戶那天他還不會走路，我很有信心地買在一個現在回頭看非常勇敢的價位。
現在他會跑會跳，會問我一加一等於幾。
帳戶那邊，數字還停在原地，連爬都還沒學會。
我本來準備了一堂很勵志的課，要講時間、講耐心、講長期的力量。
看來我得先教他另一課：大人也會做出很有把握、但完全不對的決定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合幫小孩開戶存股、結果小孩長得比帳戶快很多的時候
variations: 他已經學會跑步了，我的帳戶還沒學會站起來。
我本來要示範複利，結果先示範了套牢。

en.content:
I opened an account for my kid, called it an education fund, figured he'd learn about compounding early.
The day I opened it he couldn't walk yet, and I confidently bought in at a price that looks extremely brave in hindsight.
Now he runs, he jumps, he asks me what one plus one is.
Over in the account, the number hasn't moved. It hasn't even learned to crawl.
I had a very inspiring lesson prepared, all about time and patience and the long view.
Looks like I have to teach him a different one first: grown-ups make confident decisions that are completely wrong.
en.editorNote: For when the kid you opened a long-term account for is growing much faster than the account
variations: He learned to run. The account hasn't learned to stand up.
I meant to demonstrate compounding. I demonstrated being underwater instead.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 台股高檔震盪、投資人長時間盯盤的市場氛圍；原創的記憶體被成本價佔滿自嘲，無任何個股或價位資訊

zh-tw.content:
我記不住家人的生日，每年都要靠手機提醒。
但我記得每一檔的成本價，到小數點第二位，不用想就講得出來。
走在路上看到車牌那四個數字，我會先在心裡讀成代號，再想那檔今天收在哪。
結帳看到三十七塊五，我會想到某一檔的成本。
我的腦袋沒有變聰明，它只是被重新裝潢過，而且動工的人不是我。
最可怕的是，這些數字裡面，沒有一個是我真正需要記得的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合腦內記憶體全被成本價佔滿、卻記不住重要日子的時候
variations: 我的腦容量有限，很不巧全拿去放成本價了。
連車牌都能自動讀成代號，這種天賦我真的不太想要。

en.content:
I can't remember my family's birthdays. My phone has to remind me every year.
But I know my cost basis on every position to two decimal places, instantly, without thinking.
When I see a four-digit license plate on the street, I read it as a ticker first, then wonder where that one closed today.
When a bill comes to 37.50, I think about what I paid for something.
My brain didn't get smarter. It got renovated, and I'm not the one who hired the contractor.
The worst part is that not one of those numbers is something I actually needed to remember.
en.editorNote: For when your entire memory has been reallocated to cost basis and none of it to real life
variations: Limited memory, and unfortunately all of it is allocated to cost basis.
Reading license plates as tickers is a talent I did not ask for.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 投資人重新檢視持股與自選股清單的市場氛圍；原創情境，不指涉任何真實個股或下市事件

zh-tw.content:
我自選股清單最上面那一檔，已經不能交易了。
它停在最後那天的樣子，價格永遠是那個數字，成交量永遠是零，連顏色都沒有。
刪掉它只要按兩下，兩秒鐘的事，我做不到。
每次滑過那裡我都會停一下，然後假裝是不小心看到的。
我留著的其實不是那檔股票，是那個還很相信自己看得懂市場的我。
它不會再有任何變化了，但我每天還是會經過它一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那檔早就沒了、卻一直捨不得從自選股刪掉的時候
variations: 刪掉只要兩秒，我已經拖了兩年。
它永遠不會再動了，我還是每天去看它一次。

en.content:
The one at the top of my watchlist can't be traded anymore.
It's frozen the way it looked on its last day: same price forever, volume always zero, no color at all.
Deleting it takes two taps. Two seconds. I can't do it.
Every time I scroll past I pause, then pretend I saw it by accident.
What I'm keeping isn't the stock. It's the version of me who still believed he could read this market.
Nothing about it will ever change again, and I still walk past it once a day.
en.editorNote: For the dead ticker you never had the heart to remove from your watchlist
variations: Two taps to delete. I've been putting it off for two years.
It will never move again, and I still visit it every day.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 台股高檔劇烈震盪、投資人盯盤時間拉長的氛圍；原創的生活場合偷看盤自嘲，不含任何行情判斷

zh-tw.content:
朋友結婚那天，司儀請大家把手機收起來，好好參與這個時刻。
我把亮度調到最低，手機藏在西裝口袋裡，每隔幾分鐘摸一下。
新人交換戒指的時候，我剛好看到那檔又跌了兩趴。
回家路上，我想得起來的不是新娘進場，是那兩趴。
我這一年不是沒有參與生活，我只是每一場都只出席了一半。
另外那一半，留在一個根本不會發現我在的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合人在重要場合、心卻整場掛在盤面上的時候
variations: 我每一場都到了，而且每一場都只到一半。
他們交換戒指的那一刻，我看到的是負兩趴。

en.content:
At a friend's wedding, the MC asked everyone to put their phones away and actually be present.
I turned my brightness all the way down, kept mine in my jacket pocket, and touched it every few minutes.
While they exchanged rings, I happened to catch that one dropping another two percent.
On the way home, what I could remember wasn't the bride walking in. It was the two percent.
It's not that I skipped my life this year. I just showed up to every part of it at half attendance.
The other half stayed somewhere that has no idea I'm there.
en.editorNote: For when you're physically at the important moment and mentally on the ticker
variations: I showed up to everything this year, at fifty percent.
They exchanged rings. I saw minus two percent.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年台股爆量期間券商下單 APP 多次當機、證交所要求擴大頻寬的新聞氛圍；內容為原創改寫的心理自嘲，不涉及任何個股、價位或行情判斷

zh-tw.content:
大跌那天，我打開下單 APP，畫面上只有一個圈圈在轉。
我重開機、切成行動網路、關掉 Wi-Fi、再重開一次，一分鐘之內做完了我這一年份的努力。
四十分鐘後系統恢復，我盯著回來的畫面，突然想不起來自己本來要按什麼。
那四十分鐘裡我一直說我很急，急著處理、急著反應、急著做點什麼。
後來我才發現，我根本沒有計畫，我只有一根很想按下去的手指。
我這一年講過的所有策略，原來斷線四十分鐘就會全部消失。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合下單系統塞車、你才發現自己只是想「做點什麼」的時候
variations: 系統恢復的那一刻，我最大的問題是：我剛剛到底要按什麼？
我以為我有策略，其實我只有一根很想按下去的手指。

en.content:
On the day everything dropped, I opened my brokerage app and got a spinning wheel.
I restarted the phone, switched to mobile data, killed the Wi-Fi, restarted again. A full year's worth of effort in sixty seconds.
Forty minutes later the system came back, and I stared at the screen with no idea what I had been about to tap.
The whole time I kept saying I was in a hurry. In a hurry to handle it, to react, to do something.
Turns out I never had a plan. I had a finger that really wanted to press something.
Every strategy I've described out loud this year can be erased by forty minutes of downtime.
en.editorNote: For when the order app freezes and you realize you just wanted to do something
variations: The second it came back online, my biggest question was: what was I about to tap?
I thought I had a strategy. I had a finger that wanted to press something.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 台股高檔震盪、帳面數字劇烈起伏的市場氛圍；生活場景（統一發票對獎）為原創對照，不含任何投資建議

zh-tw.content:
這期發票我對中兩百塊。
我在家庭群組發了訊息，還加了三個驚嘆號，晚餐主動說我請。
同一天，我的帳面數字比上個月少了一趟本來說好的旅行。
這件事我一個字都沒提。
兩百塊會變成今天的晚餐，那趟旅行只會變成一個「我明天再看」的畫面。
我不是不會算數，我只是很清楚哪一種錢真的會進到我口袋。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合中了小獎超開心、卻假裝沒看到帳面浮虧的時候
variations: 中兩百塊我請客，虧掉一趟旅行我沉默。
我很清楚哪一種錢是真的，只是我只在兩百塊的時候承認。

en.content:
I won twenty bucks on the receipt lottery this month.
I posted it in the family chat with three exclamation marks and offered to cover dinner.
That same day, my account was down by roughly one of the trips we'd been planning.
I didn't bring that part up.
Twenty bucks becomes dinner tonight. The trip just becomes a number I'll look at tomorrow.
It's not that I can't do math. I just know exactly which kind of money actually reaches my pocket.
en.editorNote: For when a tiny win makes your whole day and the paper loss never gets mentioned
variations: Twenty bucks and I'm buying dinner. A whole trip gone and I say nothing.
I know which money is real. I just only admit it at twenty bucks.

items.sourceNote: 2026/08 台幣走弱、跌破關鍵價位的市場背景；內容為原創改寫的自嘲，只談投資人心理，不做任何幣別或標的建議

zh-tw.content:
今年我在美股很認真：熬夜盯盤、看財報、進進出出十幾趟，選股選到眼睛痠。
同一時間，台幣一路走弱，而我對這件事完全沒有做任何事。
年中結算，我把美金換算回台幣，發現整個帳戶居然還是正的。
拆開來看才明白：我操作的那部分是負的，匯率那部分是正的，而且比較大。
我今年唯一穩定的收益來源，是一個我完全沒有參與、也完全看不懂的東西。
現在我跟朋友說我「擅長總體經濟」，其實我只是剛好站在那裡沒動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合發現自己賺到的錢跟自己的努力完全無關的時候
variations: 我操作的那部分是負的，我沒參與的那部分是正的。
我今年最會賺的技能，叫做站著不動。

en.content:
This year I took my overseas account seriously: late nights, earnings reports, a dozen trades, picking until my eyes ached.
Meanwhile my home currency slid all year, and I did absolutely nothing about that.
At the halfway mark I converted everything back and the total was somehow still positive.
Broke it down: the part I traded was negative, the currency part was positive, and it was bigger.
My only steady source of gains this year was something I had zero involvement in and don't really understand.
Now I tell friends I'm 'good at macro.' I just happened to be standing there, not moving.
en.editorNote: For when the money you made has nothing to do with anything you did
variations: The part I traded was negative. The part I ignored was positive.
My most profitable skill this year was standing completely still.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年資金大量從傳統穩健商品湧入市場的氛圍；儲蓄險解約情節為原創改寫，重點在投資人對「慢」的雙重標準，不建議任何人解約或申購任何商品

zh-tw.content:
我有一張繳了八年的儲蓄險，一年大概幫我長兩趴。
去年我覺得它太慢了，慢到我快睡著，於是我認賠解約，把錢整包搬進市場。
我還跟家人解釋：這叫做讓錢去比較有效率的地方工作。
今年我的帳面，一年少了三成。
一樣都是等，兩趴的時候我說我沒時間，三成的時候我說我很有耐心。
我沒有變得比較會投資，我只是換了一個比較貴的地方，學同一件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回頭看自己當初「嫌它太慢」的那個決定的時候
variations: 兩趴我嫌慢，三成我說我在等它。
我沒有變會投資，我只是把學費繳到更貴的地方去。

en.content:
I had a savings policy I'd been paying into for eight years. It grew about two percent a year.
Last year I decided that was too slow — slow enough to put me to sleep — so I ate the surrender fee and moved the whole thing into the market.
I even explained it to my family as sending the money somewhere it could work more efficiently.
This year my account is down about thirty percent.
Both situations are just waiting. At two percent I said I didn't have time. At minus thirty I say I'm very patient.
I didn't get better at investing. I just found a more expensive place to learn the same lesson.
en.editorNote: For when you revisit the decision you made because something felt too slow
variations: Two percent was too slow. Minus thirty percent, and suddenly I'm patient.
I didn't get better at investing. I just pay tuition somewhere pricier now.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 心情板的日常自嘲情緒分享；行動電源與看盤習慣的對照為原創改寫，只談使用手機的行為，不涉及任何標的、價位或市場方向

zh-tw.content:
今年我最果斷的一筆消費，是一顆行動電源。
店員問我要幾毫安培的，我說有多大買多大。
他以為我要去環島，其實我只是想撐過一個下午。
我的功課沒有做得比較多，只有我的手機最清楚，我一天到底打開它幾次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合午餐都還沒吃完、手機就跳出低電量提醒的那個下午
variations: 別人的行動電源是為了旅行，我的是為了刷新。
我的手機電池老得比我快，因為它一天要被點亮一百次。

en.content:
Power banks — I bought the biggest one on the shelf without blinking.
The clerk assumed I travel a lot. I don't. I just need my phone to survive an afternoon of me opening the same app every four minutes.
My research didn't get any better. My phone is simply the only one who knows how many times a day I unlock it.
en.editorNote: For the afternoon your phone hits low battery before you've finished lunch
variations: Power banks are for hikers, campers, and people who refresh one screen all day.
Battery health drops faster than mine. It gets woken up a hundred times a day.

items.sourceNote: 維基百科「投資心理學」條目關於非理性決策與心理帳戶的概念；賣場比價情節為原創改寫，只呈現同一個人在不同場合的雙重標準，不含任何投資建議

zh-tw.content:
我可以站在冰櫃前面三分鐘，比較兩瓶牛奶哪一瓶比較划算。
回到家，我用不到十秒鐘，就把一筆夠買一整年牛奶的錢，交給一個我只知道名字的東西。
我不是不會算，我只是算的地方不太一樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在賣場貨架前突然意識到自己雙標的那一秒
variations: 賣場裡的我很精明，打開軟體的我很豪爽，這兩個人從來沒見過面。
我對一包衛生紙的研究，比對我最大一筆持股還深入。

en.content:
Grocery aisle math is where I'm a genius: three minutes at the fridge door comparing two cartons of milk, unit price and all.
Then I got home and moved a year's worth of milk money in under ten seconds, into something I knew by name and nothing else.
I can do math. I just do it in the wrong aisle.
en.editorNote: For the second you catch yourself squinting at a unit-price sticker
variations: Coupon me and portfolio me have never once been in the same room.
I research toilet paper harder than I research my largest position.

items.sourceNote: 維基百科「沉沒成本」條目關於反覆確認與難以放手的行為描述；牙醫情節為原創改寫，重點在忍不住一直查看的習慣，不涉及任何標的或市場判斷

zh-tw.content:
牙醫幫我補完牙，交代了一句：那裡已經處理好了，你不要一直用舌頭去頂它，它不會因為你一直關心就好得比較快。
我很誠懇地點頭，說我懂。
走到停車場，我坐在車上，把同一個畫面又刷新了一次。
有些道理我在診所裡聽得很懂，走出大門就自動失效。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛剛才對自己說「今天不要再看了」、結果五分鐘後又打開的時候
variations: 我的舌頭跟我的手指，是同一種毛病長在兩個部位。
醫生說不要一直去碰，我說好，然後那天碰了七十次。

en.content:
Dentist finished the filling and told me: it's handled, stop poking it with your tongue, it will not heal faster because you keep checking on it.
I nodded very sincerely and said I understood.
Then I sat in the parking lot and refreshed the same screen again.
Some advice makes perfect sense inside the office and expires the moment I walk out the door.
en.editorNote: For five minutes after you promised yourself you were done looking for the day
variations: Tongue and thumb: two body parts, one disorder.
He said stop touching it. I said sure, and then touched it seventy times.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 工作板的職場人際尷尬情境；同事聚餐座位的情節為原創改寫，刻意不寫講了什麼內容，只寫社交後果，不含任何推薦或投資建議

zh-tw.content:
上個月同事問我：「你不是都在研究這個嗎，有沒有什麼想法？」
我很熱心，講了整整十分鐘。
這個月部門聚餐，我特地挑了離他最遠的位置。
他也很有默契，整晚沒有問我任何事。
我們現在有一種很成熟的相處方式，叫做互相都不提。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合部門聚餐前一晚，突然想起自己上個月講太多的那種心情
variations: 熱心十分鐘，尷尬一整年。
他沒有怪我，這件事比他怪我還難受。

en.content:
Coworker asked me last month what I thought, since I'm supposedly the one who follows this stuff. I talked for ten straight minutes.
Department dinner this month, I picked the seat farthest from him.
He didn't ask me a single question all night.
We now have a very mature working relationship, built entirely on never bringing it up again.
en.editorNote: For the night before a team dinner, when you remember how much you said last month
variations: Ten minutes of enthusiasm buys you a full year of avoiding one person.
He never blamed me once. Somehow that is the worse version.
